channel.title: The African Street Journal
channel.description: Daily news from all 55 African countries, every source cited.

item.title: Sierra Leone regulator reports NLE 7.4 million in 2024 revenue
item.description: The electricity and water watchdog collected the money from levies and licenses, up from NLE 2.3 million in 2023.

item.title: Sierra Leone analysis questions vice president’s path to presidency
item.description: A political economist argues the office has often lacked a clear succession route, citing Solomon Ekuma Berewa’s 2007 election defeat.

item.title: Sierra Leone charcoal trade sustains burners as tree loss threatens food security
item.description: A 65-year-old burner says his family depends on the work, while the environmental agency warns that economic trees are being cut.

item.title: Liberia task force alleges US$1.2 billion in annual gold smuggling
item.description: PORT chairman Abraham Kromah says gold leaves the country outside tax collection, while residents demand records of recoveries and prosecutions.

item.title: Monrovia mayor-designate proposes US$14.5 million city plan
item.description: James K. Mulbah’s six-part agenda includes a digital revenue registry, waste collection zones and a drainage programme with the public works ministry.

item.title: Tunisie Freelance holds client payments until work is approved
item.description: The Tunisian platform says it has more than 34 000 members and lets businesses fund a job without paying the freelancer upfront.

item.title: Cabo Verdean musician Morgadinho dies in Paris at 95
item.description: The composer and former member of Voz de Cabo Verde wrote “Crioulo na França,” a song associated with emigration and ties to the diaspora.

item.title: BAI joins Luanda Semba Sound Festival on 28 November
item.description: The Angolan bank is linking the event to its 30 years of activity and says it will support the promotion and preservation of cultural heritage.

item.title: Togo assigns road company maintenance target of 1 700 km for 2027
item.description: The target is in the 2027-2029 programme budget, while the government has not specified the cost of the work.

item.title: EU tightens pesticide limits for Egyptian produce from January 2027
item.description: The rules follow 91 EU notifications on Egyptian shipments from January to August, 81% of them involving pesticide residues.

item.title: Namibia wrestlers seek N$334 600 for Commonwealth championships
item.description: The federation needs the funds by 27 November for accommodation, meals and a training camp in Polokwane, South Africa.

item.title: Juba council arrests 14 over soak pit violations in Hai Sujun
item.description: Enforcement teams are stepping up action against homes and businesses that discharge wastewater onto public streets.

item.title: Western Equatoria trains 619 police recruits for 2027 elections
item.description: The recruits, including 37 women, are training at three sites as police prepare to secure polling stations instead of the army.

item.title: Mauritius banks raise lending rates by 0.25%
item.description: MCB’s prime lending rate is 7.15% from 23 November, while Absa’s rose to 7.95% on 18 November.

item.title: Botswana's diamond naming campaign faces US regulatory hurdle
item.description: Lab-grown diamond producers are invoking the US Federal Trade Commission's existing guidance as Botswana seeks to distinguish mined stones from laboratory-made alternatives.

item.title: Chad's communication minister ranked 13th among Africa's 100 most influential young lea...
item.description: Gassim Chérif Mahamat, 40, enters the Choiseul 100 Africa 2026 list, which recognises 200 young public and private sector leaders across the continent.

item.title: Moroccan-origin groups press Spain parties for voter representation
item.description: The campaign comes as Vox calls for a review of naturalizations involving more than 300,000 Spanish citizens of Moroccan origin.

item.title: Credaf Group names Massetou Traoré chief executive
item.description: The Abidjan-based financial holding company says she will lead its seven Alios Finance subsidiaries operating in seven African countries.

item.title: Saudi ambassador plans Sierra Leone visa centre for workers
item.description: The proposed centre would handle visa applications and biometric services, while a training facility would prepare prospective workers for Saudi jobs.

item.title: Botswana's road toll reaches 189 deaths, with tire failures uncounted
item.description: Crashes killed 189 people and seriously injured 448 between January and September 2026, including 165 fatal crashes, according to the assistant transport minister.

item.title: Aeon extends pre-seed round to $2 million for African cyber defence
item.description: The Nigerian cybersecurity company added investment from Launch Africa Ventures and Octerra Capital after raising $1 million in September.

item.title: Mauritius proposes committee on offences by children
item.description: The parliamentary inquiry would examine causes, parental responsibility, support services and whether to change the minimum age of criminal responsibility.

item.title: Libyan command vows response after two naval staff die in Benghazi attack
item.description: The General Command said the officers died from injuries sustained in an attack on Benghazi Port and explosions involving the targeted vessel.

item.title: Botswana Power Corporation seeks 33% tariff rise for April 2027
item.description: The proposal would lift average commercial rates from P2.11 to P2.76 per kilowatt-hour, with no government subsidy to cushion customers.

item.title: Endeavour Mining backs Gontougo development plan as mine construction starts
item.description: Vision Tanda links the Assafo-Dibibango gold project to local jobs, businesses, living conditions, education and training.

item.title: Burkina Faso insurance centre graduates 261 professionals
item.description: The graduates completed insurance diploma and certificate programmes, while the training centre plans specialist modules in risk management and digitalisation.

item.title: Malawi's ruling party spokesperson says rules let Chakwera seek 2030 nomination
item.description: Jessie Kabwila says the Malawi Congress Party's members wrote its rules and have the power to agree on Chakwera's candidacy.

item.title: Algeria targets 2028 end to fertiliser imports as phosphate mine starts
item.description: The government says the Bled el Hadba project will supply domestic fertiliser and support non-hydrocarbon exports after an investment of nearly 5.3 billion dollars.

item.title: Rwanda weighs avocado export plans at three-day industry meeting
item.description: Growers, exporters and officials are reviewing production, quality and market access as Rwanda seeks more foreign exchange from avocados.

item.title: Simelane runs 120km to support Eswatini renal patients
item.description: The Royal Eswatini Sugar employee finished a solo route from Siteki to Lavumisa in under 24 hours, with funds raised still to be tallied.

item.title: Tunisie Telecom pays 46.1% of state firms’ 2025 distributions
item.description: The telecom operator contributed 49.7 million dinars of 107.9 million, while total distributions fell 73% from 2024.

item.title: CAF names Mané and Gueye among five African player finalists
item.description: Senegal has two contenders, while Morocco leads with three; the winner will be announced at the CAF Awards in Lagos on 2 December.

item.title: Guinea’s government sets out results-focused approach after retreat
item.description: Prime Minister Amadou Oury Bah says ministries will coordinate projects, track delivery and settle cross-government issues at senior level.

item.title: Zambia-Lobito railway advances to preferred bidders
item.description: The proposed line from Chingola to Luacano has partial African Development Bank funding, but its economic case remains the question.

item.title: Gloer Investments competes for Africa business awards in Johannesburg
item.description: The Zimbabwean engineering and energy firm reached the final stage after ranking first in the national leg of the competition.

item.title: South Sudan rules out forced evictions as it maps six national parks
item.description: The government will consult residents, verify land claims and negotiate any relocation under proposed guidance for protected areas.

item.title: Africa’s Green Economy Summit lists 20 projects seeking over US$500 million
item.description: The deal books include a Kenyan proposal to reuse electric motorcycle batteries as stationary energy storage systems.

item.title: Juba academic proposes China-South Sudan governance research centre
item.description: Dr. Jackline Benjamin Libo Warille says it would link universities to produce policy advice and train public servants.

item.title: Togo's lawmakers approve creation of deposits fund in first reading
item.description: The proposed institution would manage public and private deposits and invest them in projects including housing, health, education, water and renewable energy.

item.title: Togo begins 16-day campaign against violence toward women and girls
item.description: The guidance covers physical, psychological, sexual, economic and online abuse, and sets out ways victims and witnesses can seek help.

item.title: Western Cape High Court sets aside Phala Phala impeachment report
item.description: The court ruled the panel had to find sufficient evidence to justify an inquiry, not merely information about the theft at Ramaphosa's farm.

item.title: Tunisia’s SECADENORD develops AI tool to cut pumping costs
item.description: Aqua Min 360 analyses water volumes and electricity use, recommending lower-tariff pumping periods and the most efficient pumps.

item.title: Obi mourns Pete Edochie, 79, for bringing Nigerian culture to global audiences
item.description: The former Anambra governor praised the veteran actor’s portrayal of Okonkwo in the television adaptation of Chinua Achebe’s Things Fall Apart.

item.title: Institutional investors hold 38.3% of Cameroon’s Treasury bonds
item.description: Their bond holdings fell by CFA19.23 billion in October, while Treasury bill holdings rose 33.6% to CFA68.89 billion.

item.title: Eswatini open schools football campaign against Mozambique
item.description: The boys’ and girls’ teams face Mozambique on December 4, then Lesotho, in a nine-nation youth tournament in South Africa.

item.title: Mozambique approves 10 new higher-education institutions in a week
item.description: Five private institutions cleared on 24 November must still win approval of their teaching plans and licences before they can open.

item.title: Sierra Leone signs US$21.9 million phone assembly deal
item.description: The agreement with Gambian company Unique Group proposes a phased facility, with training, device testing and repairs included.

item.title: China pledges to continue medical mission in Burkina Faso
item.description: At a Ouagadougou anniversary, the Chinese ambassador announced a second team for the country’s economic capital after 17 missions.

item.title: Senegal seminar examines management of borders with Gambia and Guinea-Bissau
item.description: Researchers and specialists met in Ziguinchor to discuss how land and maritime boundaries can support peace and cooperation among the three countries.

item.title: Tanzania and Cuba advance university research cooperation
item.description: Universities in both countries are implementing collaboration under agreements that include a 2023 framework between Dar es Salaam and Havana.

item.title: Nachtigal takes 80.8% of climate funding in Cameroon review
item.description: Three financing operations for the 420 MW plant totalled $48.2 million, within a government sample of 80 operations.

item.title: Tebboune names Karim Zaghib to lead Algeria's lithium-battery factory
item.description: The Algerian scientist, who spent 28 years at Hydro-Québec in Canada, will transfer his expertise to build battery manufacturing at home.

item.title: Congolese bank BGFI RDC finances subcontractor CMD with $45 million
item.description: The loan to CMD, a Congolese subcontracting firm, is expected to create more than 300 new jobs, according to the bank.

item.title: Yogo’s Toubou chiefdom traces more than 125 years of local rule
item.description: The Niger community near Chad’s border has had five chiefs since its official creation in 1900, with a new leader elected in 2025.

item.title: Algeria takes 133 cruise passengers to five sites near Algiers
item.description: Le Champlain called at Algiers after Annaba, with a tour spanning the capital's landmarks and Tipasa's UNESCO-listed archaeological site.

item.title: Malawi construction regulator appoints acting chief as CEO moves to university
item.description: Board chair Peter Matipwiri says Gerald Khonje’s secondment to teach at Mubas took effect immediately under a letter dated November 23.

item.title: High Court summons Mombasa police chief over unexecuted KSh154.4 million debt warrant
item.description: Justice Jairus Ngaah ordered OCS Eliud Kimwele to explain why officers have not arrested Finance Executive Evans Oanda under a warrant received in June.

item.title: South Africa deports Zimbabwean after suspended sentence over Ukraine plans
item.description: Wesley Sothole, 24, pleaded guilty to planning to travel to Ukraine; four other Zimbabweans arrested with him have yet to enter pleas.

item.title: Kenya's I&M Bank launches metal card with global lounge access
item.description: The Mastercard World Elite card adds travel and medical insurance, concierge support and curated hotel and lifestyle offers to its benefits.

item.title: Niger reports 81 flood deaths and 131 injured by 31 October
item.description: Floods also affected 97 334 people and destroyed 12 985 homes, according to the population ministry’s representative.

item.title: South Sudan pitches investors on farming, livestock and fisheries
item.description: At a trade forum in Ethiopia, Trade Minister Labanya Margret Mathya cited land, livestock and a fisheries sector she said could earn US$300 million annually.

item.title: Dutch Embassy in Cairo closes public premises amid demonstrations
item.description: The Foreign Ministry ordered a temporary shutdown, and the embassy says it will notify people with existing appointments about rescheduling.

item.title: Eastern Province reports nine cholera cases in two districts
item.description: Four cases are confirmed, with reports covering Chipata and Kasenengwa, according to the provincial briefing.

item.title: Highlanders end strike and commit to two fixtures
item.description: The players had refused to travel for a league match amid unpaid salaries, bonuses and allowances; the club says the union accepted its offer.

item.title: Europe's development bank opens Abidjan office and pledges 250 million euros
item.description: The bank says the new commitments will add to more than 200 million euros it has already invested in Ivory Coast, where it began operating in 2025.

item.title: Cameroon closes candidate filings for February 2027 elections
item.description: Elections Cameroon received at least 200 files from 27 parties in Yaoundé, while parties submitted candidacies across the country.

item.title: Supreme Court allows Graça Machel to be called in Mondlane trial
item.description: The defence of former presidential candidate Venâncio Mondlane sought her testimony in the case over violence during post-election protests.

item.title: CHADEMA demands Lissu’s release before reconciliation talks
item.description: Deputy chair John Heche says the party will also require a mediator acceptable to both sides and talks on constitutional and electoral reforms.

item.title: Fernando Leite Couto Foundation schedules Maputo book fair
item.description: The eighth edition of its LER É UMA FESTA ("Reading Is a Party") book fair runs from 1 to 5 December, featuring launches of two literary works and appearances by Mozambican.

item.title: Study projects N$313.74 billion annual GDP contribution from Namibia oil
item.description: A Standard Bank Namibia-commissioned study ties the estimate to three offshore projects, while production has yet to begin and local benefits are not assured.

item.title: Boakai to sign US$5.7 billion Bea Mountain power and roads deal
item.description: The plan promises 270 MW of new generation, US$230 million for the grid and a 146 km road, with lawmakers next to decide whether to ratify it.

item.title: Gondja festival seeks business links for Chad’s second-hand clothing trade
item.description: Organisers launched the festival’s second edition in N’Djamena, aiming to connect wholesalers and retailers and raise the trade’s profile.

item.title: Opposition coalition backs Catholic leaders over religious restrictions
item.description: The Coalition Article 64 condemned a blocked Mass in Kinshasa and restrictions on Lubumbashi’s archbishop before a march over church land.

item.title: Nigeria Governors’ Forum distances itself from Paris Club refund dispute
item.description: The dispute centres on $100m, though the available report does not say what that figure covers, who is seeking the refunds, or which governments are involved in the matter.

item.title: Zimbabwe drought puts at least 40% of cattle herd at risk
item.description: A Cabinet update links the El Niño drought to pressure on farmers, while Treasury projects growth will slow to 1.2% in 2027.

item.title: Meatco proposes three-month wage cuts as exports remain suspended
item.description: The state-owned processor says a 50% reduction in working hours from January would save about N$16.7 million, while December pay also faces cuts.

item.title: Malawi nurses warn shortages threaten deliveries and emergency surgery
item.description: The nurses’ organisation says missing medicines, anaesthetics and intravenous fluids put patients and health workers at risk across the country.

item.title: Tanzania’s planning commission signs five-area pact with ODI Global
item.description: The UK-based organisation will work with the commission on research, development financing, monitoring and institutional capacity.

item.title: Mundubile and Zulu face December trial over election posts
item.description: The opposition leader and his former running mate pleaded not guilty to two sedition counts after claiming on Facebook they won the August election.

item.title: Tayebwa backs UWA’s expanded forest role and seeks resources
item.description: The deputy speaker pledged Parliament’s support as the wildlife authority takes over central forest reserves and seeks a helicopter for its operations.

item.title: Pharmacists from eight countries gather in Maputo for congress
item.description: About 300 delegates are meeting as the Portuguese-speaking pharmaceutical congress returns to Mozambique's capital after 11 years.

item.title: Benin’s media ministry seeks 24.38% budget increase for 2027
item.description: The proposed CFA12,39 billion allocation includes funding for audiovisual production, professional training and wider broadcast coverage.

item.title: Obaigbena says he received no police invitation over First Bank dispute
item.description: The chairman of THISDAY (Nigerian newspaper group) and ARISE (Nigerian television network) says settlement talks with First Bank and GHL are continuing after a Supreme Court.

item.title: Guinea court clears former minister Zenab Dramé in Nabayagate case
item.description: The ruling concerns allegations of more than 200 billion Guinean francs in misappropriated public funds; her lawyers are weighing defamation suits.

item.title: Madagascar deputies prepare to elect assembly president after 112 vote to oust Siteny
item.description: Six lawmakers are being discussed as possible successors, while negotiations and candidate filings continue ahead of Wednesday’s vote.

item.title: Madagascar and Djibouti sign three accords and discuss port cooperation
item.description: The talks included proposals for training, digitised logistics and transport infrastructure, while Madagascar’s delegation visited Doraleh terminal.

item.title: Liberia's justice ministry plans legal redress after split jury in child rape trial
item.description: Eight jurors voted to acquit Patrick Weefur and four to convict, leaving a case involving a 13-year-old girl without a verdict.

item.title: Liberian-founded IT firm KaynTech weighs expansion into Liberia
item.description: The Minneapolis company, set up about a year ago by Kromah Alhaji, sells IT services to U.S. businesses and may later open jobs in Liberia.

item.title: GMet forecasts 39°C heat in northern Ghana and southern storms
item.description: Bolgatanga and Nalerigu are expected to reach 39°C, while dawn mist and fog could cut visibility across coastal, forest and mountain areas.

item.title: Nairobi county launches 16-day campaign against gender-based violence
item.description: Activities across all 17 sub-counties will link residents with survivor support, justice, healthcare and psychosocial services.

item.title: GTEC freezes new PhD accreditation applications after universities admit students
item.description: Eduwatch backs the move to protect doctoral standards but says earlier oversight could have prevented students from starting programmes under scrutiny.

item.title: Benin’s Economic and Social Council urges stronger reporting of violence against women
item.description: Abdoulaye Bio Tchané says laws and nationwide sessions need to be matched by prevention, easier reporting and support for victims.

item.title: Niger's Tiani summons advisory council after Chad protests expulsions
item.description: The council is due to meet on 1 December as Chad condemns the collective expulsion of Mahamid civilians and calls for case-by-case review.

item.title: Sambi rejects UAE evacuation terms as Comoros talks continue
item.description: The jailed former president seeks guarantees on treatment and his return, while officials left Moroni without an agreement after a November visit.

item.title: Boulos reviews U.S. Eritrea policy after Cairo talks
item.description: The U.S. Africa envoy met Eritrea’s foreign minister three months after beginning the review, amid persistent rumours of a secret sanctions deal.

item.title: Stellenbosch selects Uganda’s Winnie Byanyima for honorary commerce doctorate
item.description: The university named the outgoing UNAIDS chief among seven recipients, citing her work on social justice, women’s rights and global inequality.

item.title: Eritrea's president leaves national unity call to proxies
item.description: A newscaster read the appeal on television, while poet Awel Said called for unity in early November.

item.title: NSRI warns visitors not to board Cape Town’s BOS400 wreck
item.description: The warning followed the rescue of an injured American tourist from rocks near Maori Bay after he was caught in rough water.

item.title: South African court postpones Sibiya case to 9 February
item.description: Investigators are seeking more time to examine four devices allegedly wiped before the former deputy police chief’s arrest and reconstruct a hotel scene.

item.title: Ghana's revenue officers arrest phone dealer over alleged GH¢1,000 mobile money bribe
item.description: The arrest followed a tax sweep at Kwame Nkrumah Circle that led officials to close 48 shops over non-compliance.
